iran.title: US using spectre of 'imaginary enemy' to frighten its people, Iran's Baqaei says
iran.text: US using spectre of 'imaginary enemy' to frighten its people, Iran's Baqaei says Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, has said that the United States is using the spectre of an “imaginary enemy” to frighten Americans. In a message posted on his X account on Saturday, Baqaei responded to US President Donald Trump’s claim about the possibility of Iranian attacks on Los Angeles and San Diego, which Trump described as “a very small price to pay". “To frighten their own people, they conjure up an imaginary enemy in the sky to overshadow the real threat on the ground,” the Iranian spokesman wrote. “The real danger lies neither beyond their borders nor in the skies over Los Angeles and San Diego. It lies in a ruling establishment that has imposed an illegal war on the world, with global consequences,” he added. To frighten their own people, they conjure up an imaginary enemy in the sky to overshadow the real threat on the ground. The real danger lies neither beyond their borders nor in the skies over Los Angeles and San Diego. It lies in a ruling establishment that has imposed an illegal war on the world, with global consequences. The U.S. president has even described the destruction of Los Angeles and San Diego as “a very small price to pay.” This is a textbook example of the politics of fear: frightening people with an imaginary threat, portraying the destruction of their own cities as an acceptable price to pay, and diverting their attention from the real danger. — Esmaeil Baqaei (@IRIMFA_SPOX) October 10, 2026

iran.title: Tehran measure to stabilise goods prices set for nationwide rollout, mayor says
iran.text: Tehran measure to stabilise goods prices set for nationwide rollout, mayor says Tehran Mayor Alireza Zakani has said that a municipal initiative to stabilise goods prices and offset the impact of US sanctions will be extended nationwide. Zakani wrote on X that despite Trump and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s "economic war on Iranians", Tehran Municipality launched the “Zero-Inflation Initiative” to freeze essential goods prices for six months. "This economic shield is set to expand nationwide to counter US pressure," he said. On Thursday, Zakani wrote on X: "Our heartfelt belief is that we are in an all-out war and must do everything in our power to reduce the economic pressure on the people. "Zero inflation" is a shield against economic warfare so that people can have greater peace of mind in meeting their essential needs." The US launched Operation Economic Outcast in late August, seeking to totally isolate Iran from international trade. People shop for produce at the historic Tajrish Bazaar in northern Tehran. (AFP)

"AU.S. military fighter jet struck the stern of Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica (also known as the “Arika Sun”) with a precision munition, fully disabling the ship’s propulsion without harming the crew," the US Central Commandposted on X. CENTCOM said the cargo vessel had attempted to transit regional waters after leaving an Iranian port.

iran.title: Centcom says four ships disabled, 135 redirected since 14 July
iran.text: Centcom says four ships disabled, 135 redirected since 14 July US Central Command (Centcom) has said it has redirected 135 commercial vessels and disabled four since the resumption of the US naval blockade against Iran on 14 July. “US forces have destroyed 10 tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ multibillion-dollar shadow network over the same period,” Centcom said on X. All mariners are advised to heed blockade warnings from CENTCOM forces. Crews should also continue to monitor Notice to Mariners broadcasts and contact U.S. naval forces on bridge-to-bridge channel 16 when operating in the Gulf of Oman and Strait of Hormuz approaches.

iran.text: By Timour Azhari and Enas Alashray RIYADH, Oct 10 (Reuters) - At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Iran-backed Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer. The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said.

north.text: With the first autumn rains falling on parts of Syria’s Jazira region (northeastern Syria) several days ago, farmers began preparing for winter plowing ahead of planting crops, particularly wheat and barley, which form a central part of the region’s agricultural activity. Plowing is one of the first stages of fieldwork. Preparing the land requires a series of operations that vary according to soil type, moisture levels, and the crop to be planted, as well as the availability of agricultural machinery and its operating costs. While farmers today rely on tractors, plows, and machinery designed to break up and level the soil, traditional tools remain in the memories of older residents who lived through a time when animals and wooden and iron implements performed most plowing work. Agricultural engineer Hassan Hamid told Enab Baladi that the timing of plowing depends on how much rain an area receives and the condition of its soil. Rainfall does not necessarily mean that all land becomes ready for plowing at the same time, he explained, because soil types and their ability to retain moisture differ from one field to another. Hamid added that some farmers prefer to wait for the first rains before bringing machinery onto their land, as moisture helps prepare the soil for cultivation. Plowing very hard, dry soil can be more difficult and costly. Conversely, taking machinery onto waterlogged land can cause the soil to clump or become compacted, making it important to assess the right timing before work begins. The agricultural engineer noted that some farmers wait after rainfall for weeds to emerge in the moist soil, then turn over or harrow the soil surface to remove them before planting. north.text: Syria ’s university admission rules have sparked anger after women were excluded from several degree programmes, including law, social sciences and business administration, prompting concerns about their access to higher education under the country’s new government. The Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research published admission requirements for the 2026-2027 academic year on 30 September. The lists allocate places at universities and technical institutes according to students' secondary-school results and preferences, while restricting admission to certain programmes based on gender. The restrictions cover military, security and civilian fields. Programmes reserved for men include legal studies at the newly established National University of Defence Sciences, as well as law, social sciences, business administration and economics at its Damascus faculties. Some technical programmes, including radio and television production at a media institute in Idlib, are also restricted to male applicants. Other affected fields include mechanical, electronic, computer, mechatronics, marine and aeronautical engineering, alongside programmes at military and security institutions. Some programmes remain open to women, including early childhood education, nursing, midwifery and selected cybersecurity courses. The restrictions vary by institution and location, and women can still study subjects such as law and engineering at other universities, including Damascus University. ukraine.title: European Commission will propose visa restrictions for Russians in January, Politico reports
ukraine.text: The European Commission is finalising plans to tighten visa rules for hundreds of thousands of Russians who visit EU countries as tourists every year, aiming to strengthen the EU's defences against hybrid attacks. Source: Politico , citing EU officials, as reported by European Pravda Details: The EU representatives said the European Commission plans to put forward the proposals in the new year after a group of countries, including Poland, Sweden and Estonia, pushed for stricter visa rules for Russians, including former combatants who fought against Ukraine. Swedish Justice Minister Gunnar Strömmer believes this system poses a threat to European security amid growing concerns about acts of sabotage, arson and other forms of hybrid warfare sponsored by Moscow. " It's obvious I think for everyone that we have vulnerabilities in our system that can be used by our enemies. As far as I understand things, the Commission is preparing a proposal that, according to what I have heard, should be launched in January next year. From a Swedish point of view, we would love to see it even earlier ," Strömmer told Politico. Strömmer welcomed the " progress " and " growing support " for introducing a stricter visa regime for Russians. Other countries plan to raise the issue at the Foreign Affairs Council meeting on 12 October and propose additional restrictions on Russian diplomats in the EU. Estonia has proposed a complete ban on entry to the EU for former members of the Russian armed forces. ukraine.title: The more Putin escalates his attacks on Europe, the more Europe should support Ukraine | Timothy Garton Ash
ukraine.text: Moscow’s imperialist strongman believes decadent European democracies can be cowed. Our job is to prove him wrong Vladimir Putin is escalating both his full-scale war against Ukraine and his shadow war against the rest of Europe . His main purpose in the shadow one is to break European support for Ukraine so he can subjugate that country, something he regards as existential for Russia’s future and his own. While we in the rest of Europe must prepare as best we can to defend ourselves against every kind of hybrid attack, the central thrust of our response should be to redouble our support for Ukraine. Ukraine is his main target. It’s there, and only there, not in a contest of a thousand hybrid pinpricks, that Putin’s Russia can in a meaningful sense be defeated and deterred. In a powerful new book, Warum Russland nicht aufhören wird (Why Russia Won’t Stop), the German historian Martin Schulze Wessel shows how Putin’s policy fits into a much older Russian tradition of territorial expansionism and striving for hegemony, combined with a religiously infused imperial ideology. He reminds us that in 2016 Putin said “Russia’s frontier ends nowhere” and in 2025, “wherever the boot of a Russian soldier steps, that is ours”. West Europeans, fondly imagining that we have consigned such brute territorial imperialism to the dustbin of history, tend to think there must be some other explanation (eg something we did “wrong”, like the eastward expansion of Nato). Finns, Estonians and Poles know better. Despite Russia’s weaknesses, the author concludes, it is “the most dangerous country in the world”. Some in Asia might question that large claim, but certainly Russia is the most dangerous country for Europe . Continue reading...

A Saudi-led coalition blamed Saturday afternoon's attack on the Houthis. It was the latest of several in the past week at King Khalid International Airport in the capital, Riyadh, and marked the deadliest attack in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the Iran war. Saudi Arabia is the world's top oil exporter, and the attacks have sent up oil prices and rattled markets. Following the attack, US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was weighing whether the United States would join Saudi strikes against the rebels. Airport operations were suspended Saturday. Authorities later extended the closure until at least 9PM. Sunday, according to Flightradar24. Also on Sunday, the Houthi-run Health Ministry said 91 Yemenis were killed and 168 injured by the Saudi-led coalition in five weeks. It said 60 percent of those killed were women and children. Mix of nationalities killed at Saudi airport The attack struck an airport complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, a regional official said on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorised to speak to the media. The Saudi statement said the dead included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said several hospitals were treating the injured. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged in a social media post that an American citizen had been killed in the attack, which he condemned. yemen.text: Many people were wounded in a blast at Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, according to two eyewitnesses and two people briefed on the matter, and travellers were evacuated from parts of the facility. One of the eyewitnesses reported seeing an explosion and then seeing multiple people lying injured on the ground inside the airport. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport. "Dozens of people were injured, most of them Saudi nationals. At least five of the injured - all Saudi nationals - are in intensive care," a source at a hospital told AFP , saying some patients were transported by helicopter. A medical source in the city told AFP that "ER doctors are being called to hospitals across Riyadh," and that "we were told we are dealing with a 'serious emergency situation'. Injured are being moved to hospitals across Riyadh", with many in critical condition. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority later confirmed the attack, saying that the Riyadh airport "was targeted in an attack on Saturday afternoon, October 10, 2026, amid continued attacks targeting the kingdom's civil aviation facilities." "The attack left several people injured, with the number still being assessed," the statement added. Western embassies have warned their citizens to avoid the airport, with Spain's embassy, in a message on X, alerting nationals to a "new attack" by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on the airport. A diplomatic source separately told AFP that the Houthis had hit the airport with a missile around 1200 GMT. The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. yemen.title: Major Saudi conferences to proceed despite deadly airport attack
yemen.text: The organisers of two major Saudi energy and investment conferences said their events will go ahead this month and reassured visitors on security, after missile attacks on Riyadh's airport left four people dead and an airliner heavily damaged this week. The attacks led to widespread flight disruptions, with people taking land routes or circuitous alternative flights. The UK, France and Germany have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh. Riyadh is sticking to plans to convene global events and trying to draw in investment even amid escalating war with the Iran-backed Houthis in neighbouring Yemen that has seen the kingdom attacked dozens of times over the past weeks. Organisers of the World Petroleum Congress, set to host top global oil executives and policymakers from Sunday to Thursday, said it would proceed as planned with foreign leaders and ministers in attendance, an email sent to delegates said. "Your comfort is our priority," it said, noting that alternative routes to Riyadh, including via a four-hour drive from Dammam on the kingdom's eastern coast, were available. Italian Energy Minister Gilberto Pichetto Fratin on Friday said he would not fly to Riyadh for the International Energy Forum Ministerial Meeting, an event on WPC's sidelines, but would participate via video link. The Future Investment Initiative, launched by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman as the kingdom's flagship investment conference a decade ago, would also proceed as planned from 26-29 October, organisers said. "Safety and well-being remain our highest priority," a statement attributed to FII CEO Maha Al Saud said. Meanwhile, the west has destroyed any political authority it once had There was a world before 7 October, 2023, and now there is a world after. yemen.title: Yemen govt say advancing against Houthis around Bab al-Mandeb
yemen.text: Yemen's military is advancing against the Houthis in areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait but has not yet secured control of the waterway, after the government launched an operation to recapture lost territory, according to military sources speaking to AFP . The Saudi-backed government last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, after the pro-Iran group seized Yemen's entire western coastline in a lightning offensive. The Houthis confirmed that government forces had attacked in the Bab al-Mandeb area, but they claimed to have repelled the assault. Sources from the military of Yemen's internationally recognised government also said Mayun Island in the heart of the strait remained in Houthi hands as fighting continued. Clashes in western Yemen, specifically around the strait, had killed at least 63 people in the past 24 hours, military sources from both sides told AFP on Saturday. Thirty-five members of government forces had been killed, while 28 Houthis had died, the sources said. Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult. On Friday, a Yemeni military source within the government confirmed to AFP that their forces had launched a "major operation" in the strait region, supported by air power from Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government. Military spokesman Yahya Saree said on Telegram that the Houthis had succeeded in "driving back the Saudi-aligned troop concentrations that attempted to advance from the direction of Lahj towards Bab al-Mandeb".
